front_matter_prompts.title: Dedication Page
front_matter_prompts.prompt:
Black-and-white coloring-book line art. Clean outlines only. No shading.
Leave a very large blank center area for dedication text (DO NOT draw text).
Add a simple thin border of vines and stars.
IMPORTANT: Do NOT draw any letters/words/symbols. Keep center blank.

overlays.content:
For Elliott & Colette—
may your imaginations always soar.

interior_prompts.title: Portal Discovery
interior_prompts.prompt: Clean black-and-white children’s coloring-book line art with bold ink outlines on white, no shading or gray. Elliott (age 4–5, short light-brown hair, gray-blue eyes, round cheeks) and Colette (age 2–3, brown hair in a small top knot, gray-blue eyes, soft toddler cheeks) must resemble the attached reference children and not generic cartoon kids; keep natural child proportions and recognizable faces. Winnie, a small tan Chihuahua–Pug mix with upright ears and a curled tail, is with them. Scene: in a forest clearing the children and Winnie discover a large swirling magical portal rising behind them toward the top of the page, with outline silhouettes of two friendly winged dragons inside while tall trees and hanging vines frame the scene.

interior_prompts.prompt:
Character bible:
Children (draw these the same way on every page):
- Elliott, age 4–5, short straight light-brown hair; big gray-blue eyes; round cheeks; friendly adventurous expression, wearing medieval tunic with belt and boots or casual explorer outfit

clean black ink line drawing suitable for coloring
Clean black outlines on white.
No shading, no gray, no gradients, no shadows.
Avoid large filled-black regions; keep interiors open for coloring.

Avoid exaggerated cartoon faces or oversized eyes.
Preserve the real facial proportions from the reference images.

FULL-PAGE COMPOSITION: dynamic vertical composition.
Elliott & Colette and Winnie
fill most of the lower two-thirds.
Key elements extend upward toward the top edge.



SCENE:
Elliott & Colette walk across a floating stone bridge.
Above them coils a long cloud-serpent dragon with whiskers and flowing mane.
Puffy clouds frame the top portion of the page.

GLOBAL SAFETY (IMPORTANT):
- No object intersections or impossible overlaps.
- Clean occlusion: if objects overlap, the front object clearly covers the back object.
- No extra limbs, no duplicated faces, no merged hands/feet.
- Keep dragons anatomically clean: one head, two wings (if winged), four limbs, one tail.
- Keep shapes simple and readable for coloring.

front.prompt:
You are drawing a full-color storybook cover illustration.
Full color, rich saturation, painterly lighting. NOT black-and-white. NOT line art.

Character bible (keep consistent with the interior cast):
Children (draw these the same way on every page):
- Elliott, age 4–5, short straight light-brown hair; big gray-blue eyes; round cheeks; friendly adventurous expression, wearing medieval tunic with belt and boots or casual explorer outfit
- Colette, age 2–3, wavy brown hair in a top knot; large gray-blue eyes; soft cheeks, wearing whimsical princess-meets-adventurer dress with floral or heart motifs
Pets (draw these the same way on every page):
- Winnie, a Chihuahua–Pug mix, tan fur; upright ears; curled tail; small size
Keep these characters consistent. They represent specific real children. Do NOT replace them with generic children or idealized animated characters. Preserve their recognizable facial structure.

Full-color, premium children’s fantasy book cover illustration.
High-end animated feature film lighting (Pixar-style fantasy cool).

COLOR DIRECTION:
- World lighting = cool twilight blues, indigo, and soft violet.
- Shadows lean blue-violet or teal, NOT brown or orange.
- Portal glow = warm golden key light with soft falloff.
- Strong warm–cool contrast between portal light and forest atmosphere.
- Background should feel cool and magical, not sepia or sunset-orange.

LIGHTING STYLE:
- Cinematic global illumination.
- Soft rim lighting separating characters from background.
- Subtle cool moonlight or sky fill balancing the warm portal light.
- Warm light affects only nearby surfaces; avoid flooding entire scene with orange.

RENDERING:
- Painterly but polished.
- Smooth gradients and volumetric glow.
- No heavy black contour lines.
- Edges defined by light and color transitions, not outlines.

HARD RULES:
- NOT a coloring book page.
- No outline-only rendering.
- No large white fill areas.
- Maintain full color depth and dynamic lighting.

Expressive faces.
Modern animated-feature aesthetic.
No watermark.


Rendering must feel like a frame from a high-end animated fantasy film.

FRONT COVER SCENE:
Elliott & Colette and Winnie in the foreground,
discovering a swirling magical portal in a forest clearing.
A large friendly dragon rises protectively behind them,
wings subtly framing the composition.
A distant castle silhouette beyond the trees.

LIGHTING:
The forest environment should be cool twilight blue and indigo.
Add subtle cool moonlight or sky glow from above/behind.
The portal emits a soft golden magical light that illuminates faces and nearby ground.
Keep warm light localized — do NOT turn the entire scene orange.
Add gentle cool-violet shadow tones in unlit areas.
